newsitem.title: USA: Fingerhut union employees sign contract.
newsitem.headline: Fingerhut union employees sign contract.

text.p: Fingerhut Cos Inc's distribution and mail division employees in Tennessee and Minnesota voted to accept the company's offer of a new three-year labor contract, Fingerhut said Monday.
Terms of the contract were not disclosed.
About 2,300 employees represented by the Union of Needletrades Industrial and Textile Employees (UNITE) voted Sunday to accept the contract.

As part of the agreement, both Fingerhut and UNITE have agreed to establish a joint Minnesota Labor-Management Committee to create a working relationship. In addition, the union has agreed to drop all charges with the National Labor Relations Board related to workers in Minnesota.

"Fingerhut and UNITE negotiated in good faith to reach a fair and equitable contract that is acceptable to union members as well as to our shareholders and customers," said John Buck, Fingerhut senior vice president of Human Resources. Fingerhut employees in Minnesota and at a Tennessee distribution facility in Johnson City, Tenn., are covered by the labor contracts. The Minnesota contract covering 1,700 employees was set to expire in six weeks. The 570 employees at the Tennessee facility had been working without a contract since February 1996.
Fingerhut is a direct-to-the-consumer marketing company selling products and services through catalogs, television and other media.
